labs.lead: Each lab starts from a concrete case, explains every decision in the workflow and comes with its .dashai session: import it into your dashAI and start exploring with the data, the split and the models already prepared.
labs.box.note: Import it in dashAI from Models, with Import session. Nothing is uploaded to the cloud: everything runs on your computer.
labs.how.step.1.d: By concept, level or task type. Each one starts from a concrete decision, not from an algorithm.
labs.how.step.2.d: Download the .dashai file and import it into dashAI. In seconds you have the complete experiment.
labs.how.step.3.d: Each step says what to do, why and what to look at, with pitfalls and questions to check what you learned.
labs.how.step.4.d: Change one decision, retrain and compare against the reference results, which come from the same workflow in dashAI.

labs.cat.empty.d: Try another word or remove the task type filter.

labs.file.h: A complete experiment in one file.
labs.file.p1: It is a dashAI session packed into a single file: the dataset, how it was split, how it was prepared, which models were trained and with what results. Whoever imports it doesn't get instructions to repeat an experiment: they get the experiment.
labs.file.p2: That is why it works for teaching. The starting point is the same for the whole class, every figure can be traced and any change can be compared against the original version.
labs.file.warn: A .dashai file contains Python objects: only import sessions from sources you trust.
labs.file.part.1.d: The dataset and which row went to training, validation and test.
labs.file.part.2.d: The converters, already fitted on the training data.
labs.file.part.3.d: Each model with its hyperparameters and its metrics on the three sets.
labs.file.part.4.d: Task, columns, seed and the versions of the libraries used.
labs.teach.lead: The labs and their sessions are designed to be used in a course, without requiring programming.
labs.teach.item.1.d: The whole class starts from the same point: the same split, the same models, the same reference figures.
labs.teach.item.2.d: Each student changes just one thing, a seed, a hyperparameter or a column, and explains what happened.
labs.teach.item.3.t: Receive the work as a session
labs.teach.item.3.d: The student exports their own .dashai session and hands it in: the teacher imports it and sees exactly what was done.

labs.item.tutorias.title: Who should we offer tutoring to?
labs.item.tutorias.summary: A program office has 50 tutoring spots for 150 students and must decide, mid-semester, who to offer them to. It closes by drafting the invitation with a generative model.
labs.item.tutorias.concepts: baseline, positive class, overfitting, class weight, explainability, sampling
labs.item.tutorias.context: Lab from the talk “dashAI as a tool for learning ML and GenAI”
labs.item.tutorias.intro: You coordinate Statistics I. The first exam is over and you have 50 tutoring spots for 150 students. In this lab you build, without programming, a model that estimates who is at risk of failing, decide how to allocate the spots and draft the invitation with a generative model.
labs.item.tutorias.learn.1: Why 76.7% accuracy barely beats the model that says “pass” to everyone (71.7%).
labs.item.tutorias.learn.2: How to check which class is the positive one before reading precision and recall.
labs.item.tutorias.learn.3: What a memorizing model looks like: F1 of 1.0000 in training and 0.5421 in validation.
labs.item.tutorias.learn.4: How class weight raises detection from 23 to 36 of the 51 people who fail.
labs.item.tutorias.learn.5: Why a variable with a gap in rates can add nothing to the model.
labs.item.tutorias.learn.6: Why a generative model answers differently each time, and how to pin it down.
labs.item.tutorias.session: When you import sesion-tutorias.dashai these six models appear already trained, with a stratified 60/20/20 split, seed 42, and imputation and scaling inside the session. Validation figures, exactly as computed by dashAI 0.11.
labs.item.tutorias.sessionNote: Recall measures the “fails” class: how many of the 51 people who fail in validation each model detects.

labs.item.tutorias.teach: Share the session with the class and ask each student to change a single decision, for example the seed or the depth of a tree, and to export their own session as the deliverable.
labs.item.tutorias.req: dashAI 0.11 or later. For module 11, a text model downloaded in Generative. No prior ML knowledge needed.
labs.item.caso-01.title: Who is going to show up?
labs.item.caso-01.summary: There are 260 people registered for a conference and three weeks to decide on catering, chairs and who to follow up with. A model estimates who will attend.
labs.item.caso-01.concepts: column types, missing values, positive class, LogLoss, cost of error
labs.item.caso-01.includes: HTML lab, 2 datasets; .dashai session in preparation
labs.item.caso-02.title: How much are we going to raise?
labs.item.caso-02.summary: The same event domain, but now the target is a number: how much will be raised in registrations.
labs.item.caso-03.title: What kind of attendee is this?
labs.item.caso-03.summary: Classify each registrant into one of several profiles, and search for the best settings of each model.
labs.item.caso-03.concepts: multiclass, macro and micro, cross-validation, Optuna
labs.item.caso-04.title: What did they say about us?
labs.item.caso-04.summary: Classify open-ended comments about an event: text as data.
labs.item.caso-05.title: How many registrations will there be in March?
labs.item.caso-05.summary: Forecast registrations over time, where the order of the data matters.
labs.item.caso-06.title: Can I trust this model?
labs.item.caso-06.summary: Audit the Case 01 session: local explanations, calibration and bias.
